conclusion_rule.expected_direction: No-high-school immigrants have larger log wage gains than college-degree immigrants.
conclusion_rule.statistical_threshold: p < 0.05 describes strong statistical evidence; p >= 0.05 with the expected direction remains weak directional support.
conclusion_rule.support_rule: Support when the focal point estimate or pattern is in the expected direction. Opposite requires affirmative evidence of a material effect in the contrary direction; an opposite-signed estimate alone is inconclusive. A non-significant result in the expected direction remains weak directional support.

analysis_path.path_description: Use the authorized wage-gain table to regress trimmed individual log wage gain on education groups, estimating the no-high-school versus college-degree contrast while adjusting for country, sex, age at last home job, age squared, and last home/U.S. job years.
preprocessing_steps: Read data/wage_gain_table.xlsx.
Verify required columns: edyrs, yearLastHomeJob, yearLastUsJob, sex, yrborn, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, country.
Drop rows missing required columns.
Require lastHomeWageAdjusted > 0 and lastUsWageAdjusted > 0.
Construct log_wage_gain as log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted).
Construct edu_group from edyrs: no_high_school <= 8, some_high_school 9-11, high_school 12, some_college 13-15, college_degree >= 16.
Construct age_home_job = yearLastHomeJob - yrborn and age_home_job_sq = age_home_job squared.
Drop rows missing constructed variables.
Compute the 1st and 99th percentiles of log_wage_gain and retain rows within those cutoffs.
Fit OLS regression with HC1 robust standard errors using college_degree as the education reference group.
Report sample flow, trimming cutoffs, education group counts, coefficient, p-value, 95% confidence interval, exponentiated percent difference, direction, conclusion class, and statistical strength.

models.formula: log_wage_gain ~ C(edu_group, Treatment(reference='college_degree')) + C(country) + C(sex) + age_home_job + age_home_job_sq + yearLastHomeJob + yearLastUsJob

models.inference_criteria: The focal claim is directionally supported if the no_high_school coefficient is positive; statistical strength is strong if p < 0.05 and weak_directional otherwise. A negative coefficient is opposite only with affirmative statistical evidence against zero in the negative direction.
models.qualification: Task1 has no restrictions. Adjusting for verified demographic, country, and timing variables and trimming extreme constructed wage gains are defensible robustness choices for the same focal contrast; the paper summary notes outlier exclusions in sample construction, and the authorized dataset contains extreme adjusted wage values.

It verifies the declared columns, constructs log_wage_gain, edu_group, age_home_job, and age_home_job_sq, applies the 1%/99% trimming rule, estimates the declared adjusted OLS model with HC1 standard errors, and reports the planned focal statistic and sample flow.

candidates.decision_summary: Task1 is high-quality. I read the original paper summary, which supports an observational individual-immigrant wage-gain design using adjusted pre- and post-migration wages and comparing education groups, including no-high-school versus college graduates. I inspected the authorized dataset: 2854 rows, 12 columns, no missing values in inspected columns, edyrs ranges 0-20, adjusted wages are positive but include extreme values, and there is no individual ID suggesting one row per immigrant with possible country/occupation grouping but no repeated-measures structure in the file. The code implements the declared adjusted OLS path: it uses only data/wage_gain_table.xlsx, verifies required columns, constructs log_wage_gain and edu_group exactly as planned, constructs age_home_job and its square, trims log_wage_gain at the 1st/99th percentiles, estimates the declared HC1 OLS formula, and reports sample flow and focal statistics. The candidate is not a semantic duplicate of shared-memory path01 because it adds prespecified trimming, and it is not path02 because it uses OLS rather than median quantile regression. No low-quality rule is triggered: Rules 1.1, 1.2, 1.4, M1-M6 were considered, but the outcome, contrast, dataset, model, controls, restrictions, and implementation are supported and materially aligned. Guardrails G1, G8, and G14 apply to the use of an adjusted robustness model and trimming: these are defensible Task1 choices rather than defects. Verification limitation: I did not execute the analysis, as required; the PDF reader provided an automatic long-document summary rather than full extracted page text.

Require required variables: edyrs, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, country.
exclusion_rules: Drop rows missing required raw variables.
Drop rows with nonpositive adjusted wages.
Drop rows with log_wage_gain outside the 1st to 99th percentile range.

focal_variable_structure.source_structure: edyrs is a continuous/integer years-of-schooling variable from 0 to 20.
focal_variable_structure.analysis_structure: Categorical education group with college_degree reference and focal no_high_school coefficient.
focal_variable_structure.information_loss: Years of schooling are collapsed into five education categories.
focal_variable_structure.justification: The focal claim is categorical, comparing never-high-school immigrants to college-degree immigrants; retaining intermediate categories avoids restricting the sample only to focal groups.

code_preflight.preflight_note: The generated Task2 code was read back. It verifies the declared columns, retains all countries including Mexico, constructs log_wage_gain and edu_group, applies the 1%/99% trimming rule, estimates the declared unadjusted OLS model with HC1 standard errors, includes no sector or region controls, and reports the planned focal statistic and sample flow.

analysis_code.notes: Run from the study root directory containing data/wage_gain_table.xlsx. The script intentionally does not reference occGroupLastHomeJob or occGroupLastUsJob.

candidates.decision_summary: Task2 is high-quality. The Task2 requirement is to use the pooled poor-country NIS/Migration Projects sample including Mexico and not control for sector, agriculture/nonagriculture, or rural/urban region. The paper summary supports the immigrant-level adjusted wage-gain design and the focal education comparison. The authorized dataset has 2854 individual rows, countries including MEX, verified edyrs and adjusted wage columns, no source/GDP/rural-urban variables, and occupation columns that the Task2 code intentionally does not use. The code reads only the authorized data file, retains all countries including Mexico, constructs log_wage_gain and edu_group as planned, applies the prespecified 1%/99% trimming allowed by the anchor for the robustness candidate, estimates an unadjusted HC1 OLS education-group model, and reports sample flow, retained countries, final n, and focal statistics. The candidate is not a semantic duplicate of shared-memory path01 because path01 is untrimmed OLS, and it differs from path02 because path02 is median quantile regression. No low-quality rule is triggered: Rules 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.6, and M1-M6 were considered; the explicit sample and no-control requirements are implemented, and the trimmed unadjusted OLS estimand remains comparable to the requested focal result. Guardrails G1, G8, and G14 apply to HC1 robust standard errors and trimming as defensible methodological choices, not disqualifying defects. Verification limitation: I did not execute the code, as required; the PDF reader provided an automatic long-document summary rather than full page text.

same_focal_claim.note: The path estimates the same no-high-school versus college-degree log wage-gain contrast required for the focal claim and Task2 comparable result.

same_dataset.note: The code reads only the authorized data/wage_gain_table.xlsx file, which contains the pooled poor-country sample as represented in the authorized inputs.

not_duplicate.note: The path differs materially from path01 untrimmed unadjusted OLS by adding prespecified trimming, and from path02 median quantile regression by using trimmed OLS.

task_completeness.note: Task2 candidate is present, specified, and has linked code, entry file, and run command.

estimand_alignment.note: The unadjusted coefficient for no_high_school versus college_degree in log wage gain directly answers the required pooled poor-country including-Mexico comparison without prohibited controls.

variable_support.note: edyrs, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, and country are verified columns; the log wage-gain transformation and education grouping are supported by the paper summary and task anchor.

sample_audit.note: The code reports starting authorized rows, retained countries including Mexico, missing-column exclusions, positive-wage exclusions, constructed-variable exclusions, trimming exclusions with cutoffs, and final model n.

restriction_justification.note: Positive wage restriction is necessary for logs; listwise deletion is tied to required variables; 1%/99% trimming is explicitly allowed for the robustness candidate and justified by extreme wage values and paper outlier-exclusion evidence.

control_justification.note: No controls are used, satisfying Task2's prohibition on sector/agriculture/nonagriculture and rural/urban region controls; the code does not reference occupation-group columns.

focal_variable_structure.note: Education is grouped to preserve the claim's no-high-school and college-degree categories while retaining intermediate categories in the model.

plan_code_consistency.note: The reviewed code implements the declared outcome, education grouping, country-retention rule, no-control formula, trimming rule, HC1 OLS inference, and focal output; no missing referenced columns were found.

method_justification.note: An unadjusted education-group OLS contrast on individual log wage gains is a coherent comparable Task2 result and complies with the explicit no-control instruction.

executable_in_principle.note: Identifiable Python code, valid task-specific entry file, output path, and run command are provided and linked to the declared Task2 analysis.
